1.explanation: The SetColorHandler.postExecute method is responsible for applying new fill and stroke colors to diagram elements. In the branch handling external labels (element.labelTarget), it always uses di['background-color'] (the fill color) when calling element.updateModdleProperties. To match embedded labels’ behavior, this should instead use the stroke color (di['border-color']), so external labels get the intended stroke color.
1.bug_scenario: When using modeling.setColor on an external label (e.g. “foo” or “bar”), the handler applies the fill color to the label text rather than the stroke color, making external labels too light. Embedded labels receive the stroke color correctly, but external labels always pick up the background‐color property.

2.explanation: The SetColorHandler class is responsible for applying fill and stroke colors to BPMN elements and their labels in its postExecute method. Inside postExecute, when an element has element.labelTarget (an external label), it always picks di['background-color'] (the fill color) to update the label’s BPMNDI "color" property. To fix the bug, postExecute must be modified so that external labels use the stroke color (di['border-color']) instead of the fill color.
2.bug_scenario: When using the modeling.setColor API on an external label (not the shape itself), the label text is updated with the element’s "fill" (background-color) rather than its "stroke" (border-color). In the screenshot, the external labels “foo” and “bar” appear in a very light fill color, making them hard to read, whereas embedded labels correctly use the stroke color.
